brief.headline: NVIDIA's filings cleared the financial-condition and supply-language checks with no threshold crossed, while networking carried 21.5% of the revenue movement on a 10.0% share, research and development fell to 8.6% of revenues, and a new counterparty-risk factor appeared alongside an 8-K creating a direct financial obligation.

threads.title: What carried the movement
threads.reading: Networking grew $18.39B, from $12.99B to $31.38B, carrying 21.5% of the total revenue movement while making up 10.0% of the prior-period base — 2.2x its weight. In the same annual filing the risk factors gained exactly one addition: commercial arrangements expose the company to counterparty risks. The filing feed shows an 8-K dated 2026-08-17 with Item 1.01, entry into a material definitive agreement, and Item 2.03, creation of a direct financial obligation; the material does not say what that agreement is, and does not connect it to the risk factor.
supporting: The financial condition check ran and nothing crossed a threshold, so no margin or earnings-composition finding was raised (Class A, Financial condition check).
Networking's growth is a reported segment line in the 10-K schedule of revenue by market, not a derived estimate (Class A, Revenue composition check, R85).
The record-revenue statement of $81.6 billion was confirmed as the highest across 63 prior reported periods (Class A/B, Management claims check).
against: A component at 10.0% of the base accounted for 21.5% of the movement, 2.2x its weight, so the reported growth is less evenly distributed than the total suggests (Class A, Revenue composition check, R85).
The one risk factor added in the year concerns counterparty exposure from commercial arrangements (Class A, Filing language check, 10-K filed 2026-02-25).
An 8-K filed 2026-08-17 reports both a material definitive agreement and the creation of a direct financial obligation; its contents are not in this material (Class A, SEC filing feed).

sources.label: 10-K segment information, schedule of revenue by market (Details), filed 2026-02-25

threads.title: How the records are framed
threads.reading: Three record statements from the earnings release were tested. One held outright: revenue for the quarter ended 2026-04-26 was the highest across 63 prior reported periods. Two came back qualified — records only within the same fiscal quarter, a comparison set of 17 periods rather than all reporting history. One of the qualified quotes cites a first-quarter figure of $75.2 billion where the period checked reported $81.61 billion; the material does not reconcile the two.
supporting: Revenue of $81.61B for the quarter ended 2026-04-26 exceeded the prior best of $57.01B (quarter ended 2025-10-26) across all 63 prior periods on file, so the record claim was marked supported (Class A/B, Management claims check).

The release's own text states the comparisons it is making — up 20% from the previous quarter and up 85% from a year ago — rather than leaving the basis implicit (Class B, earnings release quoted in the Management claims check).
against: Two of the three tested record statements were qualified: a record only within the same fiscal quarter, against 17 same-quarter periods and a prior best of $44.06B, not across all periods (Class A/B, Management claims check).

A quoted record statement cites first-quarter revenue of $75.2 billion while the figure reported to the SEC for the quarter checked was $81.61 billion; the material does not explain the difference (Class B release, Management claims check).
7 of 10 management claims were not testable against filed figures (Class A/B, Management claims check).

threads.title: Spend ratio and a stable filing
threads.reading: Research and development expense fell from 9.9% to 8.6% of revenues, a 13.4% move in the ratio against a rule that flags anything above 8% in either direction. The material gives no absolute R&D figure, so whether spend rose or fell cannot be read from this — only the share. Around that, the filing looks stable: no risk factors removed, the single-source supply language crossed no threshold, and the only closed-period revisions on file date to 2016.
supporting: Zero risk factors were removed year over year; of 24, one was added, 16 modified and 7 left unchanged (Class A, Filing language check).
The single-source supply language check ran and nothing crossed a threshold (Class A, Single-source supply language check).

The only restatements found are from 2016, both upward and small: net income for the period ending 2016-07-31 raised from $253M to $261M (+3.2%) and for 2016-05-01 from $196M to $208M (+6.1%), with 484 figures on file and 0 new to the ledger (Class A, Restatements check, SEC XBRL company facts).
against: R&D as a share of revenues fell 13.4%, from 9.9% for the year ended 2025-01-26 to 8.6% for the year ended 2026-01-25, past the 8% flag (Class A, R&D share check).
16 of 24 risk factors were modified in the year, so most of the section was reworded even though none was deleted (Class A, Filing language check).
No absolute research and development figure is present in the material, so the ratio move cannot be separated into a numerator effect and a denominator effect (Class A, R&D share check).

sources.label: 10-K, R&D expense as a share of revenues, filed 2026-02-25

brief.corroboration: The Class F material is press and vendor self-publication — headlines on customer price increases above 15% and on a multi-billion-dollar license to an AI startup, plus a company blog post, a company social-media post and a third-party code repository — and it points at pricing and at commercial commitments in the same period the filing added a counterparty-risk factor and an 8-K reported a direct financial obligation. None of it can establish that any of those are related, or settle any amount; the 8-K's own contents are the only thing that would.
not_checked: 7 of 10 management claims from the earnings release were not testable against filed figures.
The contents of the 8-K filed 2026-08-17 (material definitive agreement, direct financial obligation) are not in the material, so the obligation it creates could not be sized or characterized.
No absolute research and development expense figure was available, only its share of revenues.
The financial condition and single-source supply language checks crossed no threshold, so no underlying detail was surfaced for either.
The Class F reports on pricing and on a license payment have no corresponding filing in this material to check them against.
The $75.2 billion figure quoted in one release statement could not be tied to a reported period in the material.
